newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Dow dip drives Australian stocks to lower end.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Dow dip drives Australian stocks to lower end.

text.p: SPI Futures 2424 -15 US 30yr 6.87 +0.04
10yrbond futs 92.500 -0.075 Gold NY 351.55 Lon Fix 349.80
*Stocks close lower after Dow drops, industrials see losses limited by NAB strength. Volume 407.27 million, value A$882.32 million, 1,120 stocks traded, 318 steady, 316 rises, 486 falls

The Australian share market closed lower on Friday after Wall Street tumbled with only an heroic performance from National Australia Bank, buoyed by Thursday's first quarter profit, preventing further losses.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was down 11.5 points at 2,423.0. March share price index futures were down 15 points at 2,424, a 1.0 point premium to the index.

Brokers said the fall had been no surprise given the Dow's showing, with National Australia Bank the only real positive news among the leaders although the smaller end of the market did see some action.
"With the Dow down 90, we have seen a kneejerk reaction which is not surprising," said head of equities at Intersuisse, Andrew Sekely.

National Australia Bank shares streaked ahead again, closing 1.7 percent higher at A$15.78 after reaching a record high of A$15.93, as investors expressed their approval of Thursday's A$582 milion first quarter net profit result.
"It's a great performance by an unusually well-managed bank," Sekely said.
With the leaders mostly quiet, Sekely pointed to the small end of the market which saw plenty of action.
"At the little end of the market there are a lot of things moving very strongly," Sekely said.

Catching the eye early was Gawler Craton gold explorer, Desertstone, whose shares spiked 42 percent higher to 85 cents as traders punted on its Lake Torrens prospect before easing back as profit takers emerged. Desertstone scrip closed three cents higher at A$0.63.
Shares in modem manufacturer, Netcomm, slipped 12 cents to close at A$0.65 cents after said it expected a first half loss due to difficult economic and computer industry conditions.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about three to two, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade was active while options trade slowed from Thursday's levels.
Total options traded 30,095 (34,245)
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 8,447 (6,641)
In other local markets, Australian bonds were dragged lower from the open as Treasuries weakened for the second successive session with short bonds the weakest.
By 5.20 p.m. (0620 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.42 percent, up from Thursday's 7.33 percent.

The Australian dollar eked out a modest bounce Friday to end a four-day run of lower closes, but was still 1/2 cent off on the week and short of key levels. The currency edged up from Thursday's US$0.7701 low as corporate and Asian support proved unexpectedly solid. But, fresh offshore offers stopped the rally short of resistance at US$0.7750, keeping the chart outlook bearish, while uncertainty over domestic interest rates ensured offshore investors preferred the U.S. dollar.
By 5.00 pm (0600 GMT), the unit had fetched up at US$0.7734/39 after struggling higher from an early US$0.7717/22 and US$0.7710/15 late here Thursday.
